newsitem.title: CHINA: China says new HK legislature ensures stability.
newsitem.headline: China says new HK legislature ensures stability.

text.p: China on Sunday hailed its controversial new Hong Kong legislature as providing an essential guarantee for the smooth return of the British colony to Chinese rule next year.

Criticism of the Beijing-backed Provisional Legislative Council, set up in the southern city of Shenzhen on Saturday, was malicious and unreasonable, the official Xinhua news agency said in a commentary carried by state newspapers on Sunday.
The birth of the provisional legislature pushed Hong Kong's existing elected body a step closer to oblivion and prompted protests from London, Washington and democratic activists in the territory.

Xinhua said British intransigence had given China no choice but to create the provisional body which will run in parallel with the existing legislature until the handover of power at midnight on June 30, 1997.

Beijing scrapped plans for a "through train" political transition that would have retained the existing legislature after Hong Kong's colonial governor Chris Patten introduced democratic reforms that widened its franchise.
Abolition of a legislature created under British law was a natural part of the end of more than 150 years of colonial rule in Hong Kong, said the commentary, published in the People's Daily.

The new 60-member provisional council, which was chosen in Shenzhen on Saturday by a China-controlled Selection Committee of 400 Hong Kong residents, enjoyed the backing of most people in the territory, it said.

"With the support of the majority of Hong Kong people, the Provisional Legislative Council will surely fulfill its duties and contribute to the smooth transition and long-term prosperity and stability of Hong Kong," it said.

Governor Patten has called the methods used to select the new lawmaking body "stomach-churning", saying a tennis club would run its affairs better. London has challenged China to let the International Court of Justice rule on its legality.
In an overnight report, Xinhua quoted members of the Selection Committee as criticising Britain for condemning the new legislature and urging London to stop making trouble.
